newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi yields to Toshiba in earnings race.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi yields to Toshiba in earnings race.

text.p: Hitachi Ltd, long the king of Japan's integrated electronics firms, was toppled from the top post in profits last year as a protracted freefall in memory chip prices hurt its earnings.
Hitachi, which sells everything from nuclear power plants to microchips, said Thursday that its parent current profit slid 35 percent to 84.3 billion yen ($726 million) in the year ended March 31.
"Sluggish chip prices dragged down the overall profit, although the heavy machinery sector managed to post a small profit," Executive Managing Director Yoshiki Yagi told a news conference.

Hitachi for the first time in more than 50 years ceded the top post in parent profits to archrival Toshiba Corp., which earlier this week announced a parent current profit of 96.8 billion yen ($834 million) for the year.
Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses from securities investments and other non-operating activities.
